paper_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Small - 2021 - Liu - Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium‐Based Solar Cells with/auto/Small - 2021 - Liu - Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium‐Based Solar Cells with.md

knowledge_points.content: Selenium-based solar cells (SsCs) using the polymer P5NH as a hole transport layer achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 4.3%, with a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 8.99 mA cm⁻², an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 858.3 mV, and a fill factor of 56.0%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The P5NH-based device shows a short circuit current (Jsc) of 8.99 mA cm-2, an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 858.3 mV, a fill factor of 56.0%, and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 4.3%.

knowledge_points.content: The P25NH-based selenium solar cell exhibits a champion power conversion efficiency of 3.4%, characterized by a Jsc of 8.12 mA cm⁻², a Voc of 736.3 mV, and a fill factor of 57.6%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The P25NH-based device exhibits a Jsc of 8.12 mA cm-2, Voc of 736.3 mV, and fill factor of 57.6%, and a PCE of 3.4%.

knowledge_points.content: The selenium solar cells utilize a conventional n-i-p sandwiched structure consisting of Indium Tin Oxide (ITO)/Tin oxide (SnO2)/Tellurium (Te)/Selenium (Se)/HTL/Silver (Ag).
knowledge_points.evidence: The sandwiched device structure of ITO/Tin oxide (SnO2)/Te/Se/HTL/Silver (Ag) is shown in Figure 2a.

knowledge_points.content: The HOMO levels of P5NH (-5.4 eV) and P25NH (-5.18 eV) are shallower than the valence band maximum of the selenium film (-5.64 eV), which facilitates efficient hole extraction from the selenium absorber to the HTL.
knowledge_points.evidence: The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) of the P5NH (-5.4 eV) and P25NH (-5.18 eV) are much higher than the valence band maximum of Se film (-5.64 eV), indicating that both P5NH and P25NH could sufficiently extract the holes from the Se films without any energy barriers.

knowledge_points.content: The LUMO levels of P5NH (-3.4 eV) and P25NH (-3.5 eV) are significantly higher than the conduction band minimum of the selenium layer (-3.8 eV), providing an energy barrier that effectively blocks electron diffusion into the HTL and reduces recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: the conducting band minimum (-3.8 eV) of the Se layer is much lower than the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) of P5NH (-3.4 eV) and P25NH (-3.5 eV), implying that there exists an energy barrier effectively preventing the diffusion of electrons into these polymer HTLs.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis shows that the application of P5NH and P25NH HTLs reduces the root mean square (RMS) roughness of the selenium surface from 29.629 nm to 20.591 nm and 21.171 nm, respectively, resulting in a smoother interface for electrical contact.
knowledge_points.evidence: The root mean square (RMS) roughness of the pristine Se surface (Figure 4a) is 29.629 nm while the RMS roughness of P5NH and P25NH covered on the Se substrate are 20.591 nm (Figure 4b) and 21.171 nm (Figure 4c), respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) reveals that P5NH-based SsCs have a recombination resistance (R2) an order of magnitude higher than P25NH-based SsCs, indicating that P5NH more effectively suppresses surface recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: the recombination resistance R2 of P5NH-based SSCs is an order of magnitude higher than that of P25NH-based SSCs. ... the result suggests that P5NH could strongly suppress the Se surface recombination.

knowledge_points.content: The higher hole mobility of P5NH (5.13 × 10⁻² cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) compared to P25NH is the primary factor contributing to smaller recombination losses and the resulting higher performance in selenium solar cells.
knowledge_points.evidence: By comparing the mobility data shown in Table S4, Supporting Information, the reason for smaller recombination losses of P5NH-based SSCs is attributed to the high mobility of P5NH (5.13 x 10-2 cm2 (V·s)-1).

knowledge_points.content: A discontinuous tellurium (Te) layer is used as an interlayer between SnO2 and Se to improve the adhesion and support the formation of well-oriented polycrystalline trigonal selenium (t-Se) films via gradient thermal evaporation.
knowledge_points.evidence: The discontinuous Te layer has been demonstrated to improve the adhesion of the following Se layers... After a gradient annealing treatment, the polycrystalline t-Se films would form.

knowledge_points.content: P5NH-based selenium solar cells demonstrate a lower dark saturation current density (J0) of 1.74 × 10⁻⁵ mA cm⁻² compared to 1.07 × 10⁻³ mA cm⁻² for P25NH-based cells, which correlates with the higher Voc observed in P5NH devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: From Table 3, the shunt resistance Rsh of P5NH-based SSCs is much larger than that of P25NHbased SSCs, and J0 of P5NH-based SSCs is lower than that of P25NH-based SSCs. [Table 3: P5NH J0 = 1.74 x 10^-5; P25NH J0 = 1.07 x 10^-3]

knowledge_points.content: Comparison with perovskite solar cells (PSCs) reveals that the lower performance of selenium-based solar cells is primarily due to significantly lower shunt resistance (Rsh) and higher dark saturation current density (J0), indicating more severe bulk and surface recombination in the selenium absorber.
knowledge_points.evidence: The Rsh of PSCs with the same HTLs is much larger than that of SsCs... The J0 of PSCs with the same HTLs is much smaller than that of ssCs, indicating that there exist more active bulk or surface carrier recombinations in the SsCs.

knowledge_points.content: Diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based polymers are selected as HTLs for selenium solar cells because they offer high carrier mobilities, good stability, and structural diversity for optimizing hole extraction.
knowledge_points.evidence: Because diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based polymers have several advantages including high mobilities, good stabilities, and good ability to extract holes, they have been widely used as the donors in organic solar cells or as the HTLs in PSCs.
